proof_note: Krawczyk inclusion: K(X) subset int(X), where after realifying w in C^4 to x in R^8, K(X) = x_0 - Y F(x_0) + (I - Y DF(X))(X - x_0) with F = F_tilde_R, X = x_0 + [-rho, rho]^8, and Y approximately DF(x_0)^{-1}. If sup_{J in DF(X)} ||I - Y J||_inf < 1 with Y invertible, then every J in DF(X) is invertible (Neumann series). Hence the root certified inside X is nondegenerate. The recorded contraction_bound is sqrt(2) times an upper bound on sup_{J in DF(X)} ||I - Y J||_inf. Each mesh point has a local Krawczyk box; this is NOT an interval-in-gamma certificate unless certificate_type is gamma_interval_tube. These certificates prove local uniqueness in the listed seed boxes/tubes. They do not prove global uniqueness, absence of external saddles, thimble dominance, or the QAOA exponent. Competitor certificates outside the seed boxes do not contradict this theorem. An interval enclosure of Phi(w_*(gamma)) is obtained by evaluating Phi_eff over the certified box X_gamma with the log(Delta_star) branch fixed by continuation along the mesh.

certificate_summary.theorem_level_A: Level A (pointwise mesh): For every gamma_i in the certified mesh (|Gamma| = 100), Krawczyk certifies a unique nondegenerate root of F_tilde(., gamma_i) = 0 in X_i, with divisor separation on X_i. Certificate type: discrete_gamma_points. Mesh uses code_gamma_negative_seed_chamber; do not read as 0 < gamma <= gamma_{-2pi} in physical positive coordinates without declaring physical_gamma_positive_with_gamma_code_equals_minus_gamma.
certificate_summary.theorem_level_B: Level B (mesh extension of analytic LOC): Together with the analytic LOC certificate near gamma = 0 (Thm 6.1 / Banach radius), the pointwise Krawczyk certificates (discrete_gamma_points) extend the verified BM24 seed branch on the sampled mesh beyond the analytic contraction radius.
